text:
Calgary won this one on the scoreboard and in the play, and the final five minutes showed why. Martin Pospisil snapped in the go-ahead goal at 15:38 of the third, a 3 percent chance that Anaheim never answered, and Yegor Sharangovich sealed it three minutes later on an 87 percent look. The Flames generated 2.33 expected goals in that period to the Ducks' 0.92, and they finished with 4.91 expected goals overall against 2.97 for Anaheim. By the quality of chances, Calgary deserved to win 61 percent of the time.

The early going was messier than the final tally suggests. Adam Klapka opened the scoring on a 3 percent snap shot, and Beckett Sennecke tied it with a wrist shot before Leo Carlsson put Anaheim up on the power play. Calgary outchanced the Ducks 1.58 to 0.81 in that first period and still trailed at the break. Aydar Suniev tied it in the second, and that was the only period Anaheim controlled by expected goals (1.24 to 1.01).

Lukas Dostal faced 35 shots and stopped slightly more than expected, which kept the Ducks close, while Dustin Wolf was steadier at the other end with 25 shots against and two goals allowed. Simon Nemec assisted on two goals, and Ryan Strome fired seven shots and logged 1.85 expected goals for during his shifts. Sennecke was named first star for Anaheim, but the better team, over 60 minutes, wore on the Ducks.
